title: 1993 AHSME Problem 14
statement: The convex pentagon \(ABCDE\) has \(\angle A=\angle B=120^\circ,\) \(EA=AB=BC=2\) and \(CD=DE=4.\) What is the area of \(ABCDE?\)

solutions.text: Place \(A=(0,0)\) and \(B=(2,0).\) The \(120^\circ\) angles and side lengths \(EA=BC=2\) give \[ E=(-1,\sqrt3),\qquad C=(3,\sqrt3). \] Thus \(ABCE\) is a trapezoid of height \(\sqrt3\) and bases \(2\) and \(4,\) so its area is \(3\sqrt3.\) Also \(CE=4=CD=DE,\) making \(\triangle CDE\) equilateral with area \(4\sqrt3.\) The total area is \(7\sqrt3.\) Thus the correct answer is B.
hints: Draw \(\overline{CE}\) to split the pentagon into a trapezoid and a triangle
The angle conditions give \(CE=4,\) so \(\triangle CDE\) is equilateral
